subproblems.title: A degree-0 unit orientation is plus or minus evaluation
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let ξ ∈ Λ_0(ℝ^P) = MultiVector P 0 (a continuous linear functional on the space Covector (Euclid P) 0 of 0-covectors, i.e. of continuous alternating maps (ℝ^P)^{Fin 0} → ℝ), and let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P with IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q (as frozen in the contract: there is an orthonormal τ : Fin 0 → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q such that either ξ(α) = α(τ) for every 0-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(τ) for every 0-covector α). Then there is s ∈ ℝ with |s| = 1 such that ξ(α) = s·α(()) for every 0-covector α, where () = (fun i => i.elim0) : Fin 0 → ℝ^P is the empty family.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ξ : MultiVector P 0) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → ∃ s : ℝ, |s| = 1 ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) 0, ξ α = s * α (fun i => i.elim0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: fact (F4) of the parent-supplied proof, used there in step 2c (the orientation of the submanifold M at y) and in step 3b (the orientation ξ_R(x) of the carrier, needed in step 4). Notation: for a 0-covector α, α(()) is its value at the empty family () := (fun i => i.elim0) : Fin 0 → ℝ^P.
1. Unfold IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: there is τ : Fin 0 → ℝ^P (orthonormal, with span(range τ) = Q; these two properties are not needed below) such that (a) ξ(α) = α(τ) for every 0-covector α, or (b) ξ(α) = −α(τ) for every 0-covector α.
2. τ = (). Indeed, any two functions Fin 0 → ℝ^P are equal by function extensionality, because there is no i : Fin 0 at which they could differ (every i : Fin 0 yields a contradiction, Fin.elim0). Hence α(τ) = α(()) for every 0-covector α.
3. Case (a). Put s := 1. Then |s| = 1 and, for every α, ξ(α) = α(τ) = α(()) = 1·α(()) by step 2.
4. Case (b). Put s := −1. Then |s| = 1 and, for every α, ξ(α) = −α(τ) = −α(()) = (−1)·α(()) by step 2.
5. In either case |s| = 1 and ξ(α) = s·α(()) for every 0-covector α, which is the claim.
proof_key_steps: Unfold IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q to get τ : Fin 0 → ℝ^P with ξ(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξ(α) = −α(τ) for all α.
Every function Fin 0 → ℝ^P equals the empty family (), so α(τ) = α(()).
Take s = 1 in the first case and s = −1 in the second; in both cases |s| = 1.

subproblems.title: H⁰-integral of a function vanishing off a measurable set that meets the domain in at most one point
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and H⁰ = μHE[0], the normalized 0-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P. Let C ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set (not assumed measurable), K ⊆ ℝ^P a measurable set, x ∈ ℝ^P, and F : ℝ^P → ℝ with F(z) = 0 for every z ∉ K. If C ∩ K ⊆ {x}, then ∫_C F dH⁰ = 1_C(x)·F(x); that is, the Bochner integral of F with respect to the restricted measure H⁰⌞C (μHE[0].restrict C) equals (Set.indicator C F)(x), which is F(x) if x ∈ C and 0 otherwise.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (C K : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (F : Euclid P → ℝ), MeasurableSet K → (∀ z, z ∉ K → F z = 0) → C ∩ K ⊆ {x} → ∫ z in C, F z ∂μHE[0] = C.indicator F x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the integral evaluations of steps 2d (with C := M, the possibly non-measurable submanifold, and K := tsupport ω) and 3c (with C the carrier and K a closed ball) of the parent-supplied proof, together with fact (F1). Notation: ∫_C f dH⁰ means ∫ f d(H⁰⌞C), where H⁰⌞C = μHE[0].restrict C; for measurable E and every set C, (H⁰⌞C)(E) = H⁰(E ∩ C).
1. (F1) H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero), and μH[0]({z}) = 1 for every point z (Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). In particular H⁰({x}) = 1 < ∞.
2. F = 1_K·F pointwise: for z ∈ K both sides equal F(z); for z ∉ K the right side is 0 and F(z) = 0 by hypothesis. Hence ∫_C F dH⁰ = ∫_C 1_K·F dH⁰.
3. Since K is measurable, (H⁰⌞C)⌞K = H⁰⌞(K ∩ C) = H⁰⌞(C ∩ K) (Measure.restrict_restrict, which needs only K to be measurable), so ∫_C 1_K·F dH⁰ = ∫_{C∩K} F dH⁰ (Mathlib setIntegral_indicator for the measurable set K). No measurability of C is used.
4. Case x ∈ C ∩ K. Then C ∩ K = {x}: the inclusion ⊆ is the hypothesis, and ⊇ holds because x ∈ C ∩ K. So ∫_{C∩K} F dH⁰ = ∫_{{x}} F dH⁰ = H⁰({x})·F(x) = F(x) (Mathlib integral_singleton for the measurable singleton {x}, and step 1). As x ∈ C, 1_C(x)·F(x) = F(x), so both sides agree.
5. Case x ∉ C ∩ K. Then C ∩ K = ∅: if z ∈ C ∩ K, the hypothesis gives z = x, hence x ∈ C ∩ K, a contradiction. So H⁰⌞(C ∩ K) is the zero measure and ∫_{C∩K} F dH⁰ = 0. For the right side: if x ∈ C, then x ∉ K (otherwise x ∈ C ∩ K), so F(x) = 0 and 1_C(x)·F(x) = 0; if x ∉ C, then 1_C(x)·F(x) = 0 by definition of the indicator. So both sides are 0.
6. By steps 2–5, ∫_C F dH⁰ = 1_C(x)·F(x) in all cases.
proof_key_steps: F = 1_K·F, so ∫_C F dH⁰ = ∫_{C∩K} F dH⁰ using only the measurability of K.
The hypothesis C ∩ K ⊆ {x} forces C ∩ K = {x} or C ∩ K = ∅.
If C ∩ K = {x}, the integral is H⁰({x})·F(x) = F(x) = 1_C(x)·F(x); if C ∩ K = ∅, it is 0, and 1_C(x)·F(x) = 0 because x ∈ C forces x ∉ K and F(x) = 0.

subproblems.title: Bump test 0-forms with prescribed value at the centre
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, z ∈ ℝ^P and a, c ∈ ℝ with a > 0 and closedBall(z, a) ⊆ U. Then there is ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) (TestFormOn U 0: a C^∞ 0-form on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U) such that (i) tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(z, a); (ii) ω(z)(()) = c, where () = (fun i => i.elim0) is the empty family Fin 0 → ℝ^P; (iii) ω(x) = 0 for every x ∉ ball(z, a); and (iv) covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ |c| for every x ∈ ℝ^P, where covectorEuclideanNorm is the Euclidean coefficient norm of SimonGMT (Chapter06/Mass.lean) used in the definition of M_W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (z : Euclid P) (a c : ℝ), 0 < a → closedBall z a ⊆ U → ∃ ω : TestFormOn U 0, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) ⊆ closedBall z a ∧ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) z (fun i => i.elim0) = c ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ ball z a → (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) x = 0) ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) x) ≤ |c|
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: facts (F2), (F3) and (F5) of the parent-supplied proof, used there in steps 4, 5 and 9.
1. (F3) For every 0-covector α, covectorEuclideanNorm(α) = |α(())|. By definition, covectorEuclideanNorm(α) = sqrt(Σ_I [I strictly monotone]·α((e_{I(i)})_{i ∈ Fin 0})²), the sum running over all maps I : Fin 0 → Fin P, with e the standard basis of ℝ^P. There is exactly one such map, the empty map, so the sum has a single term (Fintype.sum_unique). The empty map is vacuously strictly monotone, and the family (e_{I(i)})_{i ∈ Fin 0} is the empty family (), since all functions on Fin 0 coincide. Hence covectorEuclideanNorm(α) = sqrt(α(())²) = |α(())|.
2. Let g be a smooth bump function centred at z with inner radius a/2 and outer radius a (Mathlib ContDiffBump z with rIn = a/2 < rOut = a; valid since a > 0). Then g : ℝ^P → ℝ is C^∞, 0 ≤ g ≤ 1, g = 1 on closedBall(z, a/2) (so g(z) = 1), and g(x) = 0 whenever dist(x, z) ≥ a.
3. Let ε₀ be the constant 0-covector with value 1 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.constOfIsEmpty ℝ (ℝ^P) (Fin 0) 1), so ε₀(v) = 1 for every v : Fin 0 → ℝ^P. Define the 0-form f(x) := (c·g(x))·ε₀.
4. (iii) If x ∉ ball(z, a), then dist(x, z) ≥ a, so g(x) = 0 and f(x) = 0.
5. (i) By step 4, {x : f(x) ≠ 0} ⊆ ball(z, a), so tsupport f = closure{f ≠ 0} ⊆ closure(ball(z, a)) ⊆ closedBall(z, a).
6. f is C^∞, since x ↦ c·g(x) is smooth and a smooth scalar function times the constant covector ε₀ is smooth. f has compact support, because tsupport f is a closed subset of the compact set closedBall(z, a). As tsupport f ⊆ closedBall(z, a) ⊆ U, f ∈ 𝒟^0(U); let ω be f regarded as an element of TestFormOn U 0. Properties (i) and (iii) hold by steps 5 and 4.
7. (ii) ω(z)(()) = c·g(z)·ε₀(()) = c·1·1 = c.
8. (iv) For every x, step 1 gives covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) = |c·g(x)·ε₀(())| = |c|·|g(x)| = |c|·g(x) ≤ |c|, using 0 ≤ g(x) ≤ 1.
proof_key_steps: In degree 0 the coefficient norm of α is |α(())|, because the only index map Fin 0 → Fin P is the empty, strictly monotone one.
Take a ContDiffBump g at z with radii a/2 < a and set ω(x) := c·g(x)·ε₀, with ε₀ the constant 0-covector 1.
ω is smooth, vanishes outside ball(z, a), has tsupport in closedBall(z, a) ⊆ U, satisfies ω(z)(()) = c, and has coefficient norm |c|·g ≤ |c|.

subproblems.title: Structure of degree-0 integer multiplicity triples
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set, and R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep U 0 as frozen in the contract: M = R.carrier ⊆ U is Borel and countably 0-rectifiable in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.1 (M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ⁰) with H⁰(M₀) = 0 and F_j : ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P Lipschitz), θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable with θ > 0 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ = R.orient : ℝ^P → Λ₀(ℝ^P) = (Λ⁰ℝ^P)* is H⁰⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable, and for H⁰⌞M-a.e. z there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M z Q (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 with H⁰) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(z)) Q. Here H⁰ = μHE[0] and μ_R = R.measure = θ·H⁰⌞M. Then: (i) M is countable; (ii) for every compact K ⊆ U, M ∩ K is finite and μ_R(K) < ∞; (iii) for every x ∈ M there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q, and ξ(x) ≠ 0; (iv) if U is open, then U ∩ spt μ_R = M.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U 0), R.carrier.Countable ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → (R.carrier ∩ K).Finite ∧ R.measure K ≠ ∞) ∧ (∀ x ∈ R.carrier, (∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 R.carrier x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q) ∧ R.orient x ≠ 0) ∧ (IsOpen U → U ∩ R.measure.support = R.carrier)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3a–3b of the parent-supplied proof (local finiteness of the carrier C and the orientation of R at every carrier point), and the non-vanishing ξ_R(y) ≠ 0, which the assembly uses to obtain spt(S − T) = {y} from point_current (b) (the supplied step 7 bounds spt(S − T) ⊆ {y} directly). This is the previously comparator-accepted declaration dor_zdm_imrep_zero_structure (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.zero_dim_minimizing_trivial-a1.imrep_zero_structure-a1), reused with its identical frozen type; its complete proof is reproduced below, including parts (i) and (iv), which the selected theorem does not use. Simon treats integer multiplicity currents only for n ≥ 1 (Ch. 6 §3, chapter-06.txt line 731), so this degree-0 argument is supplied in full from the definitions: countably n-rectifiable, Ch. 3, 1.1 (chapter-03.txt lines 13–16); approximate tangent space, Ch. 3, 1.4 (chapter-03.txt lines 77–87); (M, θ, ξ), Ch. 6, 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–753); H⁰ is counting measure (chapter-02.txt line 787). Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, H⁰ = μHE[0], μ_R = R.measure = (H⁰⌞M).withDensity θ.
1. Facts about H⁰. H⁰ = μH[0] (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero). H⁰({z}) = 1 for every point z (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton), and H⁰(S) ≥ 1 for every nonempty S (one_le_hausdorffMeasure_zero_of_nonempty). Points are Borel, so for a finite set F, H⁰(F) = Σ_{z∈F} H⁰({z}) = #F (sum_measure_singleton). Compact sets are closed, hence Borel.
2. (i) M is countable. R.rectifiable gives M₀ with H⁰(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j. If M₀ were nonempty, step 1 would give H⁰(M₀) ≥ 1. So M₀ = ∅. The space ℝ⁰ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 0) has exactly one point, since two functions on the empty index set Fin 0 are equal. So each range F_j is a subsingleton, hence countable, and M ⊆ ⋃_j range F_j is countable.
3. (ii) Let K ⊆ U be compact, hence Borel. By withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict, μ_R(K) = ∫⁻_K θ d(H⁰⌞M) = ∫⁻_{K∩M} θ dH⁰ = ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ =: I, and I < ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult K. So μ_R(K) < ∞. Next, θ(z) ≥ 1 for z ∈ M (R.mult_pos, θ is ℕ-valued). Hence H⁰(M ∩ K) = ∫⁻_{M∩K} 1 dH⁰ ≤ I < ∞ (setLIntegral_mono' on the Borel set M ∩ K). Suppose M ∩ K were infinite. For every m ∈ ℕ it contains a finite F with #F = m (Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq), so m = H⁰(F) ≤ H⁰(M ∩ K) by step 1 and monotonicity. Taking m = ⌈r⌉ shows H⁰(M ∩ K) ≥ r for every real r ≥ 0, so H⁰(M ∩ K) = ∞, a contradiction. Hence M ∩ K is finite.
4. (iii) Let p(z) be the property '∃ Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M z Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(z)) Q'. R.orients says p(z) holds for H⁰⌞M-a.e. z. Since M is Borel, this means H⁰(N) = 0 for N := {z : z ∈ M and not p(z)} (ae_restrict_iff', ae_iff). If some x ∈ M failed p, then {x} ⊆ N and 1 = H⁰({x}) ≤ H⁰(N) = 0, a contradiction. So p(x) holds for every x ∈ M. Now fix x ∈ M, and take Q and τ : Fin 0 → ℝ^P from IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. Then either ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all 0-covectors α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α. Let α₁ be the constant 0-covector with value 1 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.constOfIsEmpty ℝ (Euclid P) (Fin 0) 1), so α₁(τ) = 1 (constOfIsEmpty_apply). Then ξ(x)(α₁) = ±1. If ξ(x) = 0 this would give 0 = ±1, so ξ(x) ≠ 0.
5. (iv) Assume U is open.
(⊇) Let x ∈ M; then x ∈ U by R.carrier_subset. Since {x} is Borel and x ∈ M, μ_R({x}) = ∫⁻_{{x}∩M} θ dH⁰ = ∫⁻_{{x}} θ dH⁰ = θ(x)·H⁰({x}) = θ(x) ≥ 1 (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, lintegral_singleton). For every neighbourhood N of x, μ_R(N) ≥ μ_R({x}) > 0. Hence x ∈ spt μ_R (Measure.mem_support_iff_forall).
(⊆) Let x ∈ U ∩ spt μ_R and suppose x ∉ M. Choose ε > 0 with B_ε(x) ⊆ U (U open). Then B̄_{ε/2}(x) ⊆ U is compact, so by (ii) F := M ∩ B̄_{ε/2}(x) is finite, hence closed, and x ∉ F. Since the complement of F is open and contains x, choose δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ∩ F = ∅, and put η := min(δ, ε/2) > 0. A point z ∈ B_η(x) ∩ M would lie in B̄_{ε/2}(x) ∩ M = F and in B_δ(x), which is impossible. So B_η(x) ∩ M = ∅ and μ_R(B_η(x)) = ∫⁻_{B_η(x)∩M} θ dH⁰ = 0. But B_η(x) is a neighbourhood of x and x ∈ spt μ_R, so μ_R(B_η(x)) > 0 (Measure.mem_support_iff_forall), a contradiction. Hence x ∈ M, and U ∩ spt μ_R = M.
proof_key_steps: H⁰ = μH[0] gives every point mass 1, every nonempty set mass ≥ 1, and finite sets mass equal to their cardinality.
The null set M₀ in the rectifiable cover is empty and each Lipschitz image of the one-point space ℝ⁰ is a point, so M is countable.
Since θ ≥ 1 on M, H⁰(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ = μ_R(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, so M ∩ K is finite.
Every point of M has positive H⁰⌞M-mass, so the a.e. orientation property holds at every carrier point; ξ(x) maps the constant covector 1 to ±1, so ξ(x) ≠ 0.
For U open, a carrier point has μ_R-mass θ(x) ≥ 1, and a point of U off M has a ball missing the locally finite set M, so U ∩ spt μ_R = M.

subproblems.title: Point currents and their support
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, x ∈ U, and ξ₀ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) = (Λⁿℝ^P)* (MultiVector P n, a continuous linear functional on n-covectors). Then (a) there is D ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (a GeometricCurrentOn U n: a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U), sequentially continuous in Simon's test-form topology) with D(ω) = ξ₀(ω(x)) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); (b) if ξ₀ ≠ 0, then every D ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with D(ω) = ξ₀(ω(x)) for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) has spt D = {x}. Here spt D is the support of Simon 6.2.11 as frozen: U minus the union of all open W with W̄ compact, W̄ ⊆ U, and D(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (ξ₀ : MultiVector P n), IsOpen U → x ∈ U → (∃ D : GeometricCurrentOn U n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, D ω = ξ₀ ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x)) ∧ ∀ D : GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, D ω = ξ₀ ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x)) → ξ₀ ≠ 0 → D.support = {x}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 6a and 7 of the parent-supplied proof: D(ω) = θ(y)·ξ_R(y)(ω(y)) is a current (part (a), with x := y and ξ₀ := θ(y)·ξ_R(y)), and S − T, which satisfies (S − T)(ω) = −θ(y)·ξ_R(y)(ω(y)), has support {y} (part (b) with ξ₀ := −θ(y)·ξ_R(y) ≠ 0; the supplied step 7 needs only spt(S − T) ⊆ {y}). This is the previously comparator-accepted declaration dor_zdm_point_current (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.zero_dim_minimizing_trivial-a1.point_current-a1), reused with its identical frozen type. The argument is stated here for an arbitrary degree n and an arbitrary functional ξ₀; the selected theorem uses n = 0, the point x := y and ξ₀ = ±θ(y)·ξ_R(y). Definitions: Simon's test-form topology (chapter-06.txt lines 170–175, frozen as TestFormOnConverges), currents Ch. 6, 2.1 (lines 192–194), support Ch. 6, 2.11 (lines 296–301, frozen as GeometricCurrentOn.support = U ∖ zeroRegion).
1. The functional. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) put L(ω) := ξ₀(ω(x)). Addition and scalar multiplication in 𝒟ⁿ(U) are pointwise, (ω + η)(x) = ω(x) + η(x) and (cω)(x) = c·ω(x), and ξ₀ is linear. So L is ℝ-linear.
2. Continuity. Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0): there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j, and for every k the k-th derivatives of ω_j converge uniformly on K to those of 0, i.e. to 0. If x ∈ K, the case k = 0 gives D⁰ω_j(x) → 0. Since ‖D⁰ω_j(x)‖ = ‖ω_j(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), ω_j(x) → 0, and by continuity of ξ₀, L(ω_j) = ξ₀(ω_j(x)) → ξ₀(0) = 0. If x ∉ K, then x ∉ tsupport ω_j, so ω_j(x) = 0 and L(ω_j) = 0 for all j. In both cases L(ω_j) → 0. Hence D := (L, continuity) is a GeometricCurrentOn U n with D(ω) = ξ₀(ω(x)) for all ω. This proves (a).
3. A test covector. For (b), assume ξ₀ ≠ 0 and let D ∈ 𝒟_n(U) satisfy D(ω) = ξ₀(ω(x)) for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Since ξ₀ ≠ 0, there is an n-covector α₀ with ξ₀(α₀) ≠ 0; otherwise ξ₀ = 0 by extensionality.
4. x ∈ spt D. We have x ∈ U by hypothesis. Suppose x lay in the zero region: x ∈ W with W open, W̄ compact, W̄ ⊆ U, and D(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Choose ε > 0 with B_ε(x) ⊆ W. Let φ : ℝ^P → ℝ be the smooth bump function centred at x with radii ε/4 < ε/2 (ContDiffBump): φ = 1 on B̄_{ε/4}(x), so φ(x) = 1, and tsupport φ = B̄_{ε/2}(x) ⊆ B_ε(x) ⊆ W is compact. Put ω(z) := φ(z)·α₀. Then ω is C^∞, being a smooth scalar times a constant, has compact support, and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ W ⊆ W̄ ⊆ U. So ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Hence 0 = D(ω) = ξ₀(φ(x)·α₀) = ξ₀(α₀) ≠ 0, a contradiction. So x is not in the zero region, and x ∈ spt D.
5. No other point lies in spt D. By definition spt D ⊆ U. Let z ∈ U with z ≠ x. Choose ε > 0 with B_ε(z) ⊆ U, and put ρ := min(ε/2, |z − x|/2) > 0 and W := B_ρ(z). W is open, and W̄ = B̄_ρ(z) (closure_ball, ρ ≠ 0) is compact with B̄_ρ(z) ⊆ B_ε(z) ⊆ U. If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, then x ∉ tsupport ω because |x − z| > ρ, so ω(x) = 0 and D(ω) = ξ₀(0) = 0. Thus D vanishes on W, so z ∈ W ⊆ zero region and z ∉ spt D.
6. By steps 4 and 5, spt D = {x}. This proves (b).
proof_key_steps: ω ↦ ξ₀(ω(x)) is linear, and it is sequentially continuous because convergence in 𝒟ⁿ(U) includes uniform convergence of ω_j itself on a compact set containing all supports.
If ξ₀(α₀) ≠ 0, a bump φ at x gives a test form φα₀ supported in any open W ∋ x with D(φα₀) ≠ 0, so x ∈ spt D.
Every z ∈ U ∖ {x} has a small ball with compact closure in U that misses x, on which D vanishes, so spt D = {x}.

subproblems.title: Erasing a point of a degree-0 triple
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set, R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep U 0 (as frozen in the contract; H⁰ = μHE[0], μ_R = R.measure = θ·H⁰⌞M, and R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(z)·ξ(z)(ω(z)) dH⁰(z)), and x ∈ M. Then there is R' ∈ IMRep U 0 with carrier M ∖ {x} such that μ_R = μ_{R'} + θ(x)·δ_x as measures on ℝ^P, and R'.action(ω) = R.action(ω) − θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) for every ω ∈ 𝒟⁰(U) (TestFormOn U 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U 0) (x : Euclid P), x ∈ R.carrier → ∃ R' : IMRep U 0, R'.carrier = R.carrier \ {x} ∧ R.measure = R'.measure + (R.mult x : ℝ≥0∞) • Measure.dirac x ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U 0, R'.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) = R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) - (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 6c–6d of the parent-supplied proof (the triple R_S with carrier C ∖ {y} is an IMRep in U representing S = T − D); the selected theorem applies this lemma with the erased point x equal to its regular point y, while inside the proof below x is the erased point and y denotes a generic point of M ∖ {x}. This is the previously comparator-accepted declaration dor_zdm_imrep_zero_erase_point (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.zero_dim_minimizing_trivial-a1.imrep_zero_erase_point-a1), reused with its identical frozen type; the measure identity is part of that type and is proved too, although the selected theorem uses only the carrier and the action identity. Simon excludes n = 0 in Ch. 6 §3 (chapter-06.txt line 731), so the argument is supplied in full from Ch. 3, 1.4 (chapter-03.txt lines 77–87; η_{y,λ}(z) = λ⁻¹(z − y), which is blowUpMap y λ) and Ch. 6, 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–753). It uses the sibling imrep_zero_structure (dor_zdm_imrep_zero_structure), parts (i)–(iii). Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero), so H⁰({z}) = 1 for every z (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton); M' := M ∖ {x}. Points and countable sets are Borel (Set.Countable.measurableSet).
1. Orientation of M' at its points. Let y ∈ M', so y ∈ M and y ≠ x. By imrep_zero_structure (iii) there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M y Q. Call the latter h: it gives finrank Q = 0 and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} f dH⁰ → ∫_Q f dH⁰ as λ → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0. We show HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M' y Q; the dimension part is that of h. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). Its topological support is compact, hence contained in some B̄_b(0). Put a := max(b, 0) + 1 > 0; then f(z) = 0 whenever ‖z‖ ≥ a. Put d := ‖x − y‖ > 0 and let 0 < λ < d/a. Then ‖η_{y,λ}(x)‖ = d/λ > a, so f(η_{y,λ}(x)) = 0. The set t := η_{y,λ}(M) is countable as an image of the countable set M (imrep_zero_structure (i)), hence Borel, and s := η_{y,λ}(M') ⊆ t. If z ∈ t ∖ s, write z = η_{y,λ}(w) with w ∈ M. Then w ∉ M' (otherwise z ∈ s), so w = x and f(z) = 0. By setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero, ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} f dH⁰ = ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M')} f dH⁰ for every λ ∈ (0, d/a). Since (0, d/a) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0, the function λ ↦ ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M')} f dH⁰ eventually equals λ ↦ ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} f dH⁰ along 𝓝[>] 0. The latter tends to ∫_Q f dH⁰ by h, so the former has the same limit (Tendsto.congr'). Hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M' y Q, and Q still satisfies IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q.
2. Construction of R'. Let R' have carrier M', multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. Check each field. (a) M' = M ∖ {x} is Borel. (b) M' ⊆ M ⊆ U. (c) M' is countably 0-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono, M' ⊆ M). (d) θ is measurable. (e) θ > 0 on M' ⊆ M. (f) For compact K ⊆ U, ∫⁻_{M'∩K} θ dH⁰ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ < ∞ (lintegral_mono_set). (g) H⁰⌞M' ≤ H⁰⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono), so ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H⁰⌞M' (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure). (h) By step 1 the orientation property holds at every point of M', hence H⁰⌞M'-a.e. (ae_restrict_iff' with M' Borel). So R' ∈ IMRep U 0 and R'.carrier = M ∖ {x}.
3. Measure identity. Since x ∈ M, M = M' ∪ {x} with M' and {x} disjoint and {x} Borel. So H⁰⌞M = H⁰⌞M' + H⁰⌞{x} (Measure.restrict_union), and H⁰⌞{x} = H⁰({x})·δ_x = δ_x (Measure.restrict_singleton). withDensity is additive in the measure (withDensity_add_measure), and δ_x.withDensity θ = θ(x)·δ_x since points are Borel (dirac_withDensity). Hence μ_R = (H⁰⌞M).withDensity θ = (H⁰⌞M').withDensity θ + θ(x)·δ_x = μ_{R'} + θ(x)·δ_x.
4. Action identity. Fix ω ∈ 𝒟⁰(U), put g(z) := θ(z)·ξ(z)(ω(z)) ∈ ℝ, and let K := tsupport ω. K is compact because ω has compact support, and K ⊆ U because ω ∈ TestFormOn U 0. (a) If z ∉ K then ω(z) = 0, so g(z) = θ(z)·ξ(z)(0) = 0. (b) M ∩ K is finite by imrep_zero_structure (ii). For each z, g is H⁰-integrable on {z} because H⁰({z}) = 1 < ∞ (integrableOn_singleton). So g is integrable on the finite union M ∩ K = ⋃_{z∈M∩K}{z} (integrableOn_finite_biUnion). Hence g is integrable on M (IntegrableOn.of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero: M is Borel and g = 0 on M ∖ (M ∩ K) by (a)), and therefore on M' ⊆ M and on {x} ⊆ M. (c) By setIntegral_union (M' and {x} disjoint, {x} Borel), R.action(ω) = ∫_M g dH⁰ = ∫_{M'} g dH⁰ + ∫_{{x}} g dH⁰, and ∫_{{x}} g dH⁰ = H⁰({x})·g(x) = g(x) (integral_singleton). Since R' has the same θ and ξ, R'.action(ω) = ∫_{M'} g dH⁰ = R.action(ω) − θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)).
proof_key_steps: At y ∈ M ∖ {x}, the blow-ups of M ∖ {x} and of M differ only at the point η_{y,λ}(x), which leaves the support of each f ∈ C_c once λ < |x − y|/a. So M ∖ {x} inherits the approximate tangent space and orientation of M at y.
The remaining IMRep fields (Borel, rectifiable, positivity, local integrability, measurability) pass to the subset M ∖ {x}.
H⁰⌞M = H⁰⌞(M ∖ {x}) + δ_x and δ_x.withDensity θ = θ(x)δ_x give μ_R = μ_{R'} + θ(x)δ_x.
The integrand θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ is supported on the finite set M ∩ spt ω, hence integrable, and splitting off {x} gives R'.action(ω) = R.action(ω) − θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)).

subproblems.title: Local form of a 0-current at a regular point
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set, T ∈ 𝒟_0(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U 0) and y ∈ reg T (regularSet T, Simon 7.4.1 as frozen in the contract, with n = 0). Then there are r > 0 with ball(y, r) ⊆ U and c ∈ ℝ with |c| ≥ 1 such that T(ω) = c·ω(y)(()) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) (TestFormOn U 0) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(y, r). Here ω(y) is a 0-covector and ω(y)(()) is its value at the empty family () = (fun i => i.elim0) : Fin 0 → ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U 0) (y : Euclid P), y ∈ regularSet T → ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ball y r ⊆ U ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 1 ≤ |c| ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U 0, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) ⊆ ball y r → T ω = c * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) y (fun i => i.elim0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 (2a–2d) of the parent-supplied proof. Notation: H⁰ = μHE[0]; for a 0-covector α, α(()) is its value at the empty family ().
1. Unfold y ∈ regularSet T (n = 0): there are ρ > 0 with ball(y, ρ) ⊆ U, m ∈ ℤ with m ≠ 0, a set M ⊆ ℝ^P with y ∈ M, and ξ : ℝ^P → MultiVector P 0 such that IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 0 M, IsOrientation 0 M ξ, and T(ω) = m·∫_M ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH⁰(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(y, ρ). (The remaining conjuncts, y ∈ spt T and the local finiteness of H⁰ on M, are not needed.)
2. (2a) Apply IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 0 M at y ∈ M: there are V ⊆ ℝ^0, an open set W ⊆ ℝ^P with y ∈ W, and ψ : ℝ^0 → ℝ^P with ψ(V) = W ∩ M (the other chart properties are not needed). The space ℝ^0 = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 0) has at most one point, since two functions on the empty index type Fin 0 are equal. As y ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), y = ψ(z₀) for some z₀ ∈ V. Every element of W ∩ M = ψ(V) is ψ(z) for some z ∈ V; then z = z₀, so the element is ψ(z₀) = y. Hence W ∩ M ⊆ {y}.
3. (2b) W is open and y ∈ W, so there is r₀ > 0 with ball(y, r₀) ⊆ W. Put r := min(r₀, ρ) > 0. Then ball(y, r) ⊆ ball(y, ρ) ⊆ U and ball(y, r) ⊆ ball(y, r₀) ⊆ W, so M ∩ ball(y, r) ⊆ W ∩ M ⊆ {y}.
4. (2c) The second conjunct of IsOrientation 0 M ξ at y ∈ M gives a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q. By the sibling unit_orientation_zero (Submission.regcomp_cop_zdr_unitOrientation_zero) there is s ∈ ℝ with |s| = 1 and ξ(y)(α) = s·α(()) for every 0-covector α.
5. Put c := m·s. Then |c| = |m|·|s| = |m| ≥ 1, since m is a nonzero integer.
6. (2d) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(y, r). As ball(y, r) ⊆ ball(y, ρ), step 1 gives T(ω) = m·∫_M f dH⁰ with f(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)). Let K := tsupport ω; it is closed, hence measurable. For x ∉ K, ω(x) = 0, so f(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0 because ξ(x) is linear. Moreover M ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ ball(y, r) ⊆ {y} by step 3. The sibling isolated_point_integral (Submission.regcomp_cop_zdr_setIntegral_eq_indicator; with C := M, which need not be measurable, the measurable set K, the point y and F := f) gives ∫_M f dH⁰ = 1_M(y)·f(y) = f(y), because y ∈ M. By step 4, f(y) = ξ(y)(ω(y)) = s·ω(y)(()). Therefore T(ω) = m·s·ω(y)(()) = c·ω(y)(()).
7. So r > 0, ball(y, r) ⊆ U, |c| ≥ 1, and T(ω) = c·ω(y)(()) whenever tsupport ω ⊆ ball(y, r), as claimed.
proof_key_steps: Unfold regularSet: T = m·[[M]] on ball(y, ρ) ⊆ U, with m ≠ 0, M a 0-dimensional embedded submanifold through y oriented by ξ.
A chart ψ : ℝ^0 → ℝ^P has a one-point domain, so W ∩ M = {y}; shrink to ball(y, r) ⊆ W ∩ ball(y, ρ), giving M ∩ ball(y, r) ⊆ {y}.
The orientation at y is ξ(y) = s·eval with |s| = 1 (unit_orientation_zero); put c := m·s, so |c| = |m| ≥ 1.
For tsupport ω ⊆ ball(y, r), the integrand ξ(·)(ω(·)) vanishes off tsupport ω, which meets M at most in y, so isolated_point_integral gives T(ω) = m·s·ω(y)(()).

subproblems.title: A local nonzero point mass forces an isolated carrier point
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set, T ∈ 𝒟_0(U), and R = (C, θ, ξ_R) ∈ IMRep U 0 with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_C θ(x)·ξ_R(x)(ω(x)) dH⁰(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U), where H⁰ = μHE[0], C = R.carrier, θ = R.mult and ξ_R = R.orient. Let y ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0 with ball(y, r) ⊆ U, and c ∈ ℝ with c ≠ 0, and suppose T(ω) = c·ω(y)(()) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(y, r), where () = (fun i => i.elim0) is the empty family. Then y ∈ C and C ∩ ball(y, r) ⊆ {y}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U 0) (R : IMRep U 0) (y : Euclid P) (r c : ℝ), R.Represents T → 0 < r → ball y r ⊆ U → c ≠ 0 → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U 0, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) ⊆ ball y r → T ω = c * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) y (fun i => i.elim0)) → y ∈ R.carrier ∧ R.carrier ∩ ball y r ⊆ {y}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3 (3a–3c), 4 and 5 of the parent-supplied proof, with the parent's local form (*), T(ω) = m·s·ω(y)(()), taken as the hypothesis with c := m·s. Notation: C = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ_R = R.orient, H⁰ = μHE[0]; for ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) put F_ω(z) := θ(z)·ξ_R(z)(ω(z)), so that T(ω) = ∫_C F_ω dH⁰.

By the sibling unit_orientation_zero (Submission.regcomp_cop_zdr_unitOrientation_zero), for every x ∈ C there is s_x ∈ ℝ with |s_x| = 1 and ξ_R(x)(α) = s_x·α(()) for every 0-covector α.
2. (Vanishing off the support.) If ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) and z ∉ tsupport ω, then ω(z) = 0 and F_ω(z) = θ(z)·ξ_R(z)(0) = 0, because ξ_R(z) is linear.
3. (3c, isolated atoms.) Let x ∈ C and a > 0 with C ∩ closedBall(x, a) ⊆ {x}, and let ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(x, a). By step 2, F_ω vanishes outside the closed, hence measurable, set closedBall(x, a). The sibling isolated_point_integral (Submission.regcomp_cop_zdr_setIntegral_eq_indicator; with the set C, K := closedBall(x, a), the point x and F := F_ω) gives T(ω) = ∫_C F_ω dH⁰ = 1_C(x)·F_ω(x) = θ(x)·ξ_R(x)(ω(x)), since x ∈ C.
4. (Step 4: C ∩ ball(y, r) ⊆ {y}.) Let x ∈ C ∩ ball(y, r) and suppose x ≠ y. Put δ := dist(x, y), so 0 < δ < r, and a₀ := min(r − δ, δ)/2 > 0; then a₀ < r − δ and a₀ < δ.
 (a) closedBall(x, a₀) ⊆ ball(y, r): if dist(z, x) ≤ a₀, then dist(z, y) ≤ dist(z, x) + δ ≤ a₀ + δ < r.
 (b) y ∉ closedBall(x, a₀), because dist(y, x) = δ > a₀.
 (c) closedBall(x, a₀) is compact and contained in ball(y, r) ⊆ U, so C ∩ closedBall(x, a₀) is finite by step 1. Hence F₀ := (C ∩ closedBall(x, a₀)) ∖ {x} is finite, therefore closed, and x ∉ F₀. As the complement of F₀ is an open set containing x, choose ε > 0 with ball(x, ε) ∩ F₀ = ∅, and put a := min(ε/2, a₀) > 0.
 (d) C ∩ closedBall(x, a) ⊆ {x}: if z ∈ C ∩ closedBall(x, a) with z ≠ x, then z ∈ closedBall(x, a₀) (as a ≤ a₀), so z ∈ F₀; and dist(z, x) ≤ a ≤ ε/2 < ε, so z ∈ ball(x, ε) ∩ F₀ = ∅, which is impossible.
 (e) Since closedBall(x, a) ⊆ closedBall(x, a₀) ⊆ ball(y, r) ⊆ U, the sibling bump_form (Submission.regcomp_cop_zdr_exists_bumpForm; centre x, radius a, value 1) gives ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(x, a), ω(x)(()) = 1, and ω(p) = 0 for every p ∉ ball(x, a).
 (f) tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(x, a) ⊆ ball(y, r), so the hypothesis applies: T(ω) = c·ω(y)(()). Since y ∉ closedBall(x, a₀) ⊇ closedBall(x, a) ⊇ ball(x, a), ω(y) = 0, hence T(ω) = c·0 = 0.
 (g) By step 3 (applicable by (d) and tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(x, a)) and step 1, T(ω) = θ(x)·ξ_R(x)(ω(x)) = θ(x)·s_x·ω(x)(()) = θ(x)·s_x. Here θ(x) ≥ 1, as θ(x) is a positive natural number for x ∈ C (R.mult_pos), and s_x ≠ 0 since |s_x| = 1; so T(ω) ≠ 0, contradicting (f). Hence x = y, which proves C ∩ ball(y, r) ⊆ {y}.
5. (Step 5: y ∈ C.) Suppose y ∉ C. Then no z ∈ C lies in ball(y, r): by step 4 such a z would equal y, giving y ∈ C. Since closedBall(y, r/2) ⊆ ball(y, r) ⊆ U, the sibling bump_form (centre y, radius r/2, value 1) gives ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(y, r/2) ⊆ ball(y, r) and ω(y)(()) = 1. The hypothesis gives T(ω) = c·1 = c. On the other hand, every z ∈ C satisfies z ∉ ball(y, r) ⊇ tsupport ω, so F_ω(z) = 0 by step 2; the integrand vanishes at every point of C, hence T(ω) = ∫_C F_ω dH⁰ = 0 (Mathlib setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero, which needs no measurability). Thus c = 0, contradicting c ≠ 0. Therefore y ∈ C.
6. Steps 4 and 5 give y ∈ C and C ∩ ball(y, r) ⊆ {y}.
